cues.text: Ambient space bed in (optional, user-supplied)
Out in the dark, far beyond the Solar System, there is a star that does not look the way stars are supposed to look.
Soft rising swell into the hook caption
Stars come in many colours, but green is almost never one of them. So what is going on?
Reveal: low gentle tone
This is WD J1330+6435, a white dwarf roughly 280 light-years from Earth. Astronomers report that its modelled colour is a pale chartreuse green.
What you see on the surface is an artistic visualization. Nobody has seen detail on a star this distant.
Transition: soft whoosh into evolution sequence
To understand the colour, we start with the life of a Sun-like star. It swells into a red giant.
Shell expulsion: slow swell
It sheds its outer layers into space, and leaves behind a hot, dense core: a white dwarf.
Transition into debris sequence
Around some white dwarfs, rocky debris from a former planetary system orbits and falls inward.
That planetary material can pollute the star’s atmosphere with elements you would never expect there.
Transition into spectrum display
Astronomers study starlight by spreading it into a spectrum. Sodium in the dense atmosphere absorbs broadly across the orange part of that spectrum.
Colour conversion: gentle rising tone
Feed that spectrum into a model of human colour vision, and the star’s apparent colour changes. That is how the green is modelled.
Transition back to the star
A white dwarf is the dense remnant of an evolved star. This diagram is a schematic, not a view inside.
A typical white dwarf is roughly the size of Earth, with about half the mass of the Sun.
Transition into the former planetary system
Here, the debris is the remains of a former planetary system. Paths and distances are illustrative.
Dust and rock, lit by the remnant’s faint light, spiral inward over time.
One last orbit around the star, and its modelled colour.
Music swell for the pullback
The universe is more colourful than we imagined.
What should we explore next?
Music resolves; fade out by 08:00
